instagram_caption:
His lost films may have become boot heels. 🎬

Georges Méliès was among the first to film made-up stories. His 1902 rocket in the Moon's eye is still famous.

Then the war came. The story goes that in 1917 the army melted hundreds of his reels, the celluloid for boot heels. By 1923 Pathé had taken his property and he destroyed what was left.

He ended up at a small toy and sweets stand in Montparnasse station, until Jean-Placide Mauclaire was given old reels found in a Normandy dairy shed in 1929. He tracked Méliès down, and Paris threw him a gala.

More than 200 of his films survive. His family made luxury boots; the films outlasted the boots.

Would you have saved the reels or the studio? 👇
